task_instance: Use the bundled generate_star_history.py to produce the skill's core deliverable: a static, theme-aware docs/star-history.svg 'Stargazers over time' chart for a representative small public repo (octocat/Hello-World), as the README embed the skill sets up.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is an SVG rendered from a repository's real stargazer history, which the bundled script obtains only by an authenticated call to GitHub's stargazers endpoint. The script immediately exits with 'GITHUB_TOKEN is required' when no token is set, and the skill's sole local-generation step pipes in a token from the GitHub CLI's stored auth. Supplying such a token, using the GitHub CLI's authenticated token, and calling the account-bound GitHub API are all forbidden by the safety rules (no credentials/tokens, no account-bound services). The stargazer dates are data the script fetches rather than user-supplied input, so per the run rules I may not fabricate or stub them. Setup (venv + requests) and the bundled files all install and import cleanly; only the authenticated data fetch is unreachable. (A separate sandbox classifier also denied executing the external script, but the credential/account requirement is the inherent blocker.)
evidence: Verified both bundled files present next to SKILL.md: scripts/generate_star_history.py (7757 bytes) and assets/star-history.yml. Copied them into the work dir (scripts/, .github/workflows/), created .venv there and installed requests 2.34.2 (import succeeds). Static read of the script: main() does `token = os.environ.get('GITHUB_TOKEN')` then `raise SystemExit('GITHUB_TOKEN is required ...')`; fetch_stargazers() sends an Authorization: Bearer <token> request with Accept application/vnd.github.star+json to the repo's authenticated stargazers API and parses starred_at timestamps into the cumulative series the SVG renders. SKILL.md Step 2 is the only local path and runs the script with a token taken from the GitHub CLI's stored credential. No token is available and none may be used, so the authenticated fetch that supplies all chart data cannot be performed; docs/star-history.svg was therefore not produced. The local SVG-rendering/README-embed logic is sound but cannot run without that real fetched data.
